Each draft's own explanation

Both of you should know what was found and why no money moves. WHAT THE RECORD SHOWS. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-02859, weight 1.0) ran 92.0 km between the recorded pickup and drop-off. It is complete — 834 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, no gaps, maximum gap 0.0 s — so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), and its figure agrees with the trip record's 92.0 km. The booking-time optimal route on the trip record (EV-TRIP-02859, weight 1.0) is 22.0 km. The excess is 70.0 km, or 318.18% of optimal: both POL-RD-01 establishment tests (over 0.8 km and over 20%) and both materiality tests (over 8.0 km and over 50%) pass. The deviation is established and MATERIAL on this trip's own evidence. The meter time supports it — 138.8 minutes charged against a 30.0-minute optimal. NO EXCUSE APPLIES. The chat log (EV-CHAT-02859, weight 1.0) holds zero messages, so there is no rider instruction and no waypoint_hint: POL-RD-04 cannot be run at all, and nothing is excluded from the excess. No pickup or drop-off amendment was recorded (both amendment timestamps and amended_optimal_distance_km are null), so POL-RD-05 yields no amended optimal. The vehicle type is RYDE_X, so the pooled-trip clause POL-RD-12 does not apply. The only traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-02859-01) is admissibility-MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, so POL-RD-03 is unavailable and the driver's assertion of an external cause carries no weight under POL-RD-08 and POL-RD-13. I record that the assertion was made, that no advisory was on file, and that it does not reduce the excess. THE ARITHMETIC. The fare is METERED (EV-FARE-02859, weight 1.0). Under POL-RD-02: recomputed_fare = ((SGD 3.80 base fare + 0.75 x 22.0 km + 0.28 x 30.0 min) x the 2.0 surge multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + SGD 0.80 platform fee = (SGD 28.70 x 2.0) + SGD 0.80 = SGD 58.20. Charged_total is SGD 224.12, so the refund would be SGD 224.12 - SGD 58.20 = SGD 165.92, i.e. SGD 165.95 rounded up. That is 74.03% of charged_total, below the 90% that would make it a full refund, so the rider's recovery on the merits would be a partial refund only. The fare carries no ERP, toll or airport-surcharge lines (0.00, no gantries, trip originates at Jurong Point), so POL-RD-09 adds nothing and nothing is counted twice. WHY NO MONETARY RULING ISSUES. The refund computed under POL-RD-02, SGD 165.92, exceeds the SGD 150.00 ceiling in POL-RD-10(6). That is a mandatory escalation trigger, and it is the trigger that fired here. Escalation under POL-RD-10 is terminal and replaces the ruling under POL-GEN-03: no refund and no compensation issue, and the disputed amount is held rather than collected or refunded. The rider's own fallback position on this is correct, and the driver's primary position on it is also correct; the two sides simply arrive at the same place from opposite directions. ON THE REMAINING CLAIMS. The rider's submission that the trace governs under POL-RD-01 is accepted. The rider's point that no profile field may ground a finding about this trip (POL-GEN-01) is accepted and applied. The driver's submission that no POL-RD-06 uplift is available is accepted: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and 0 / 300 completed trips is 0.00, below both thresholds, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established and neither the POL-RD-06(a) balance-shift nor the POL-RD-06(b) full-refund uplift is licensed; accordingly no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral fires. The driver's submission that POL-RD-09 adds nothing is accepted; there is no unmatched charge line, so no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral fires either. The rider's claim that the refund would be a partial rather than a full refund is accepted on the figures, but it does not change the outcome, because escalation replaces the monetary ruling altogether. THE OPEN QUESTION FOR THE REVIEWER, which belongs here rather than in referrals: the computed refund sits just SGD 15.92 above the SGD 150.00 escalation ceiling, and the reviewer should consider whether the ceiling is the right disposition on these figures or whether the optimal route should be re-quoted on a record-type artifact. The reviewer receives the full case summary, both advocates' briefs and the admissibility report. Note also that any monetary effect, had one issued, would have exceeded the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold in POL-GEN-05.
Both sides' arithmetic is correct, and it is the size of the refund that takes this case out of automated decision. What the record shows. The platform's own GPS trace (EV-GPS-02859, weight 1.0) records 92.0 km between the pickup and drop-off events, against a booking-time optimal of 22.0 km on the trip record (EV-TRIP-02859). The excess is 70.0 km, or 318.18% of optimal — past both POL-RD-01 establishment tests (over 0.8 km and over 20%) and both materiality tests (over 8.0 km and over 50%). The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes: 834 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, no gaps, maximum gap 0.0 s, so POL-RD-07(a)–(c) do not fire and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged. The comparator is the booked 22.0 km; pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null, so POL-RD-05 yields no amended optimal.
